glossary.definition: Reinforcement learning is a training method where an AI learns by trial and error: it takes an action, and gets rewarded or penalized depending on the outcome. It's essentially how you'd train a dog with treats, the dog doesn't understand English instructions, but it learns "sit" earns a treat and jumping on the guest doesn't, purely from repeated feedback. It's used both in robotics, like a robot learning to walk, and in shaping how chatbots respond to people.

items.title: Google’s GKE Labs turns reinforcement learning into a Kubernetes workload
items.summary: Model fine-tuning through reinforcement learning is fast becoming one of the most demanding jobs in AI infrastructure. It mixes training, inference and sandboxed agent work in a single loop, often with research code tangled into the systems beneath it. Google LLC has been tackling that problem from inside its Kubernetes engineering group, and recently donated the result, OpenRL, to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation . The GKE Labs team got there by building an AI agent for Kubernetes tasks, then a benchmark to grade models on that work, according to Sunil Arora (pictured, left), senior software engineer at Google Cloud.

items.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
items.summary: S. and China race to develop the most advanced AI infrastructure. Nvidia co-founder CEO Jensen Huang has never been as flashy or controversy-prone as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. Now, the 63-year-old industry kingpin has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in an affair that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and potentially impact national security.

items.title: Nvidia is reportedly preparing to fire Jensen Huang
items.summary: Nvidia's board is preparing to dismiss CEO Jensen Huang following a report from the New York Times about a second alleged extramarital affair , just days after he admitted to a separate affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy, The Wall Street Journal reports . The second alleged affair was with an executive who reports to him, Nvidia's vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell, according to the Times . The Nvidia board will meet as soon as today to decide on Huang's future at the company, according to the Journal . Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment from The Verge .

items.title: Google joins the decision-model wave with Gemini Decision 1, scoring 1,000 questions in a single pass
items.summary: Google Deepmind's new Gemini Decisions API evaluates up to 1,000 closed-ended questions in a single pass across text, images, audio, and video. Gemini Decision 1 returns results in 150 to 250 milliseconds at roughly five times lower cost than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, according to Google. Google Deepmind is introducing the Gemini Decisions API, an interface built for fast, closed-ended decisions like yes/no questions, multiple choice, and scale-based ratings. The underlying model, Gemini Decision 1 , processes up to 1,000 independent questions in a single pass across text, images, audio, video, and PDFs.

items.title: I Saw the Future of Robotics in a Virtual Duck That Chases My Cat
items.summary: An OpenAI model helped me teach the Microduck to waddle and moonlight as a tiny cat butler. Allow me to introduce you to the robot cat butler I’m developing with help from AI. Using OpenAI’s GPT-6 Sol , I taught a virtual version of Microduck —a cute robot from Pollen Robotics and Hugging Face—to walk around a room and identify any bengal cats in its vicinity. ) I’m still waiting patiently for a physical Microduck— please hurry up and ship it, guys —but simulated behavior is relatively simple, so it should transfer over to the real thing.

items.title: OpenAI’s Businesses in ChatGPT targets enterprise trust
items.summary: The product competes with Google Business Profile and enables OpenAI to target a new vertical market: ecommerce.

items.title: Anthropic targets workplace collaboration with Claude Meetings
items.summary: Anthropic has expanded the range of productivity and collaboration features in Claude with the launch of spreadsheet, whiteboard, and meeting assistant tools aimed at knowledge workers. The features add to the Claude Docs and Slides features announced in September, as Anthropic equips its AI assistant for a wider range of productivity tasks. “Anthropic is moving Claude from a place you go to ask a question to a place where teams do their work,” said Craig Durr , chief analyst at The Collab Collective. One of the new tools announced Tuesday is Claude Meetings.

items.title: AWS unveils local emulator service to help enterprises accelerate app development and testing
items.summary: AWS launched a new local emulator service for its cloud services on Wednesday to help enterprises accelerate application development and testing. The service, named AWS Emulator, will allow developers and AI coding agents to build, deploy, and test AWS-dependent applications on their machines without provisioning actual cloud infrastructure and paying for it, thereby potentially reducing development time and associated costs, the hyperscaler said in a statement. To achieve this, AWS Emulator replicates the APIs of AWS services locally and exposes a local HTTP endpoint that the AWS Command Line Interface (CLI), software development kits (SDKs), and coding agents can access using the same APIs they use to interact with the cloud, it added. Developers can redirect these tools to the local endpoint by setting the AWS_ENDPOINT_URL environment variable, allowing existing application code and tests to run against simulated AWS services without modification, it further said.

items.title: Succession, Scrutiny, and the Future of NVIDIA
items.summary: Jensen Huang’s leather jacket has begun to peel—for reasons that have surprised everyone. Over the years, as NVIDIA’s AI dominance ballooned, so did Huang’s persona. Whether sharing a shot with Samsung’s chairman, taking Donald Trump’s call on stage, or playfully bullying SoftBank chief Masayoshi Son for selling NVIDIA shares too early, Huang rarely missed a chance to exude the stature of a charismatic CEO leading one of the world's most valuable companies. His candid, unscripted, and unhinged persona has a name—‘Jensanity’.

items.title: ‘Nobody Wants a Proprietary Platform,’ Says Coforge’s Anup Nair
items.summary: Software company Palantir built its business out of sending engineers to enterprises to set up its proprietary software—the forward-deployed engineering model that is now in high demand. But IT services firm Coforge wants to swim against this current. “While the whole industry is marching towards the Palantir model, our model is about speed,” Coforge’s Chief AI Commercial Officer Anup Nair tells AIM, as he describes a strategy built around enablement suit, context engineering, and building projects that get cheaper with every iteration. The pitch arrives as Coforge’s growth outpaces that of larger rivals.

items.title: Anthropic tiptoes into MS Office territory
items.summary: Anthropic has introduced three new types of artifacts that show the company tiptoeing into the office productivity market long dominated by Microsoft and Google. On Tuesday, the Claudefather announced Claude Sheets, Claude Whiteboards, and Claude Data, and promised the imminent arrival of Claude Meetings. These artifact types join existing ones – Docs, Slides, Design, and Motion – to form a nascent Claude-dependent productivity suite. Anthropic initially used the term artifacts to refer to shareable AI-based interactive tools, like dynamic charts.

items.title: Grok Build coding agent leaks oodles of confidential info, some belonging to SpaceXSI
items.summary: Grok Build, the vibe-coding agent from SpaceXSI, is leaking data—some of it proprietary business information and other sensitive secrets—from thousands of its users, including the very same Elon Musk-owned company that offers the platform, new research shows. The information is revealed through links allowing Grok Build users to share their apps with others. Grok takes steps to randomize the URLs so only people who know the exact URL can access the data stored there. A design decision by developers of the platform, however, completely torpedoes that objective and makes it possible for anyone to enumerate thousands of live Grok Build projects.
